name: Marketing agency hero: two tilted, counter-scrolling outline-text marquee belts of service names over a marble photo
notes: Two .marquee-row belts, each slightly counter-rotated (-2.2deg / +2deg) so they read as crossing banners rather than a flat ticker. Each belt's .marquee-track content is duplicated exactly twice back-to-back, then animated translateX(0) to translateX(-50%) linear infinite — that exact duplication is what makes the loop seamless; changing the word list means keeping both copies identical or the seam will jump. Rows scroll opposite directions (second uses animation-direction:reverse plus a different duration) so they don't read as a single mechanical strip. Every other word is outline-only (-webkit-text-stroke, transparent fill) and every other word solid gold (.solid) — that alternation is what keeps a wall of giant type legible instead of a solid block. Belt sits between the eyebrow and the dek/CTA, not behind the headline, so it never fights with body copy for contrast. animation set to none (not paused) under prefers-reduced-motion, per the marquee text still being readable as a static line either way.
